newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products steady to higher, gas oil jumps.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products steady to higher, gas oil jumps.

text.p: Med oil products were mostly steady to higher on Wednesday with gas oil rallying.
Gas oil jumped sharply on strong arbitrage demand to Asia and tight supply of heating oil grades, traders said.

Alpine was the first to take advantage of the arbitrage, fixing 50,000 tonnes to load out of Constanza on Nov 10-12 bound for India. A good part of India's 550,000 tonne December tender could be covered from the Med if enough product in major ports could be found, dealers said.
Sentiment was further buoyed by Turkey's tender to buy 100,000 tonnes 0.5 percent gas oil in the second half of Nov.
That brings the country's demand for the month as a whole to 225,000 tonnes.

Fuel oil was steady, still showing strength against the North. A high sulphur cracked NWE cargo that sold at $120.50 cif Brindsi on Tuesday helped the move to push quotes higher, but several dealers thought the price a touch high estimating the mid teens as a more represenative level.
Some traders felt low sulphur cracked fuel would rise, but there was little sign of this on Wednesday with offers understood to have been made in a $127-129 cif Med range.
Gasoline prices were steady to lower.
Premium unleaded cargoes were at $232/$233 cif, down $1.
Traders said the Med appeared well balanced but demand in eastern Med destinations should support prices, as well as signs the arbitrage to the U.S. may be close to open.
Naphtha was also unchanged at $216/$218 cif with a Skikda cargo believed on offer, but the price was unknown.
Two large Skikda cargoes of about 60,000 tonnes each, to be loaded Nov 1-10, were believed headed out of the Med to northwest Europe.
One industry source said Brazil may be interested in purchasing one of them.
